column6: Read-first note: this part rests on source reads of community bridges, not Apple documentation
Pass anything but the full monotonic position_ids and KV lands at the wrong cache slice — logits stay plausible
No WWDC transcript is cited anywhere in this part — nothing here has Apple-session backing
Signature-trust scope note — verify against your checkout before relying on anything below
TOC: asset-generation coverage is not numerical parity — a bundle that generates is not one that computes correctly
The bridge's core call is private AIProgram._from_mlir_module — any coreai wheel bump can break it without notice
mlx2coreai pins coreai-core b1; b1 bundles fail on Xcode 27 beta 3+ with 'Failed to convert to versioned IR'
The console script omits --batch-size while the Python function accepts batch_size and raises for anything but 1
_write_tokenizer rmtree's an existing destination — a re-run silently destroys whatever was there
A position_ids max that isn't the last query position writes KV to the wrong offset — valid math, wrong cache
The precision flag mutates the loaded model in place — converting several variants in one process reuses mutated weights
Skip the bf16→fp16 logit cast and the Swift runner's hard-coded Float16 view reports garbage argmax — no crash
Omitting metadata_version defaults it to '0.1' and the reader throws unsupportedVersion — write the string '0.2'
A .aimodel path where a bundle dir is expected throws pointedAtModelAsset — guarding a misleading version error
mlx2coreai writes only kind:'llm' — no VLM path exists; use Apple's exporter or swift-lm for vlm bundles
Conversion succeeds while silently listing unresolved tensors in metadata['unresolved_extra_inputs'] — read it every time
allow_unknown_sources=True (default) invents scalar fp32 specs for unknown tensors — converts fine, can be badly wrong
Capture runs the model twice (trace plus reference) — RNG or dropout diverges unless capture_is_training=False
generate_composite_decl mutates the caller's dict in place — reuse carries state you didn't put there
Shape-dependent Python branches produce two divergent traces and the probe raises — no data-dependent branching
The two backends differ by one (steps vs steps+1) under --grow-context — two hand-written copies of one contract
Generated assets are not numerical parity — tolerances compare against MLX's own capture, never a Core AI execution
match_by_order=True pairs outputs positionally — a shifted output order gives a green comparison of the wrong tensors
Never run an iOS-compiled bundle on a Mac — it can wedge the GPU/ANE stack into a watchdog reboot
Boolean attention masks are lowered as added, not selected — masked positions leak in, output stays plausible
General transposed convolution lowers to zeros — converts, runs, and outputs all-zero feature maps
mx.log2 and mx.log10 lower to natural log — every value wrong by a constant factor, no error
--runtime-backend auto silently picks Swift on Darwin unless a Python-only flag flips it — runs measure different backends
CoreAILanguageModels.ModelConfig (bundle config) is not the similarly named model configuration — name collision
The two prompt paths have opposite image-placeholder requirements and the same error case
Every Core AI test in the repo passes without running — green because skipped, not because it works
expectFrequentReshapes requests a reshape-tolerant specialization — on a static graph it costs the fast path
The community zoo is single-author, benchmarks self-declared uncontrolled — process guidance, not Apple fact
Core AI conversion is not byte-deterministic (measured) — never verify a pipeline by hashing artifacts
metadata.json can embed your build machine's absolute paths — the zoo shipped one; audit what you emit
Cite BENCHMARKS.md as a protocol, not a dataset — n=1 numbers on specific hardware
Thermals move numbers 2.3–4.1× — a day of device use silently degrades a 25 ms op; benchmark cold and hot
A community helper defaults to cpu_only() — copied code silently runs ~9–10× slower; it's the parity option
Store only the load_function and the AIModel gets GC'd — calls return garbage that looks like a conversion bug
Guided generation needs logits and the GPU-pipelined fast path never exposes them — fastest backend, no structured output
Code comment: check metadata['unresolved_extra_inputs'] after every conversion — success ≠ all inputs resolved
No WWDC transcript is cited in this guide — the 2026 session corpus does not cover these bridges
